# GOV.UK Design System styles

Page structure and visual styling: the spacing and type scales, the grid, colour, links,
lists and the page template. Read these before writing any CSS of your own.

| Style | Also called | What it is for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Colour](colour.md) | palette | Always use the GOV.UK colour palette |
| [Font override classes](font-override-classes.md) |  | Use paragraphs for your core content |
| [Headings](headings.md) |  | Use headings to structure content on pages |
| [Images](images.md) |  | Only use images if there’s a real user need |
| [Layout](layout.md) |  | Organise the layout of the page into blocks |
| [Links](links.md) |  | Use links to navigate between pages |
| [Lists](lists.md) |  | Use lists to make blocks of text easier to read, and to break information into manageable chunks. |
| [Page template](page-template.md) | boilerplate | Template combines the boilerplate markup and components needed for a basic GOV.UK page |
| [Paragraphs](paragraphs.md) |  | Use paragraphs for your core content |
| [Section break](section-break.md) |  | Break up sections of content |
| [Spacing](spacing.md) | margin, padding | The Design System uses a responsive spacing scale which adapts based on screen size |
| [Type scale](type-scale.md) |  | The type scale underpins all of the text styles on GOV.UK |
| [Typeface](typeface.md) |  | If your service is on the service.gov.uk subdomain you must use the GDS Transport font |
